The codebook assigns online_rct to online-panel experiments, whereas the paper describes a supervised session.

Under the form-spec.md Counts in prose rule, these n_randomized fields should be null, with 20 retained as the recruited count in prose. The two conditions involve the same sample; the pathway-analysis n is not stated.

corrections.form_value: Twenty designers (13 professional UX designers, the rest design students) each did two 10-minute online design sprints, drawing causal pathway diagrams in Miro, once with a plugin that includes GPT-4 suggestions and once without it. The order of the plugin condition and of the sprints was randomized within person. The paper compares self-reported ease and confidence, time on task, and the number of pathways in each diagram with paired t-tests.
corrections.source_says: Replace the statement that each of the twenty designers did two sprints with: Twenty people were recruited and asked to complete two sprints; all except one completed both, and the remaining participant completed only the no-plugin sprint. Appendix A identifies the participant who completed only one sprint as P15. The form correctly acknowledges this exception elsewhere.
corrections.quote: All participants except one completed both design sprints. One participant had to leave early due to personal reasons and only completed one of the design sprints (one without the plugin).
corrections.locator: PDF p. 6, Section 4.2; PDF p. 16, Appendix A, Table 1 and its asterisk note

confirmed: The source is arXiv:2403.08111v1 [cs.HC], dated 12 Mar 2024, in CHI 2024 author-copy format with DOI 10.1145/3613904.3642179; the title and all six author names match the form (PDF p. 1). The file contains 20 PDF pages, although its ACM reference-format paragraph says 19 pages.

The full markdown was read through the end, including Appendices A-C. The appendices contain demographics, the study protocol, and plugin screens, with no additional numerical effect estimates (PDF pp. 16-20). No separate supplementary document is identified in the paper.

There is one empirical user study: a one-hour within-person session with two planned 10-minute design sprints, one with the plugin and one without. Both plugin-condition order and design-sprint order were randomized (PDF p. 6, Section 4.1; PDF p. 16, Appendix B.3).
The intervention uses GPT-4 with temperature 1 and max_tokens 256 and bundles AI recommendations with non-AI diagramming, checking, and help features (PDF p. 6, Sections 3.1.4-3.2).

The recruitment count is 20 people, not diagrams, ideas, or ratings; all except one completed both conditions, and the exception completed only the no-plugin sprint (PDF p. 6, Section 4.2; PDF p. 16, Table 1). This supports fewer than 50 people regardless of the unreported quantitative analysis count.

The main text reports 13 professional UX designers, with the others enrolled in design-related programs (PDF p. 6, Section 4.2). Appendix A lists P9 as a pharmaceutical scientist, so its occupation entries should not be treated as a separate confirmation of enrollment status (PDF p. 16, Table 1).

The outcome counts CPD pathways produced by each designer and is analyzed with paired sample t-tests; fluency, category_count, participant, and with_ai are supported. Correctness and usefulness are self-rated confidence, not independent ratings of creative output (PDF p. 7, Section 4.4).

The reported pathway means are M_without_plugin = 1.47 and M_with_plugin = 2.32, p < .05, exactly as the form records (PDF p. 9, Section 5.2.1). Figure 4b displays pathways explored, and its caption identifies the bars as standard errors (PDF p. 10, Figure 4).
The time means are M_without_plugin = 603(s) and M_with_plugin = 556(s), p > 0.5, matching the one-line finding (PDF p. 9, Section 5.2.1).

No explicit pathway-test sample size, t statistic, degrees of freedom, numerical standard error, or standard deviation is supplied. Keeping n_analyzed and outcome n_units null is supported; the self-report tests print t(18) for ease measures and t(17) for confidence measures (PDF pp. 7, 9-10, Sections 4.4 and 5.2.1 and Figure 4).

has_randomized_people_study is true: randomized within-person AI assistance was evaluated using fluency scored on produced diagrams. The paper belongs in the requested two-screener pipeline, while core = no, criterion_2_at_least_50_people = not_met, and context_class = none remain supported (PDF pp. 6-7 and 9; creativity-codebook.md Sections 3 and 6).
This is an original user study, not a synthesis; there are no pooled estimates, confidence intervals for pooled effects, or synthesis standardizers to extract (PDF Sections 4-5).
summary: A randomized within-person study of 20 recruited designers measured output fluency and belongs in the two-screener pipeline, while failing the 50-person core threshold. Corrections concern the design subtype, randomized-count provenance, completion wording, company affiliation, and omitted code URL; the reported result numbers match the PDF.
